## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Koṭasimbalijātaka* (Ja 412) is a canonical birth story belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework recorded on SuttaCentral, the Buddha delivered the tale while residing at Jetavana to rebuke sin, addressing five hundred monks in the House of the Golden Pavement who were overwhelmed by lustful thoughts [SuttaCentral]. Urging them to exercise caution where distrust is warranted, the Buddha compared the growth of defilements around a person to banyans and parasitic plants overtaking a tree; he then recounted a tale of the past wherein a tree-spirit dwelling in the upper canopy of a silk-cotton tree (*koṭasimbali*) became terrified after seeing a bird excrete ingested banyan seeds into the branches, dreading the eventual destruction of her dwelling [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral lists four translations across four modern languages for this jātaka [SuttaCentral].
